candidates.title: ProfInfer: An eBPF-based Fine-Grained LLM Inference Profiler
candidates.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) move from research to production, understanding how inference engines behave in real time has become both essential and elusive. Unlike general-purpose engines such as ONNX Runtime, today's LLM inference systems offer little operator-level visibility, leaving developers blind to where time and resources go. Even basic questions -- is this workload memory-bound or compute-bound? -- often remain unanswered. To close this gap, we develop a fine-grained, non-intrusive profiling framework for modern LLM inference engines, exemplified by llama-cpp but applicable to similar runtime architectures. Built on extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF) technology, our system dynamically attaches probes to runtime functions across multiple layers -- without modifying or recompiling the source. It transforms collected traces into rich visualizations of operators, graphs, timelines, and hardware counter trends, exposing how dense inference, Mixture-of-Experts routing, and operator offloading behave in practice. With less than 4% runtime overhead and high profiling fidelity, our framework makes LLM inference both transparent and diagnosable, turning performance profiling into a practical tool for optimization, scheduling, and resource-aware deployment.
candidates.reason: llama.cpp等のLLM推論エンジン向けにeBPFで演算子レベルの細粒度プロファイリングを行うProfInferを提案し、メモリ律速か計算律速かといった推論基盤の計測を可能にしており、推論計測への直接貢献が確認できる。

candidates.title: Compressing LLMs with MoP: Mixture of Pruners
candidates.abstract: The high computational demands of Large Language Models (LLMs) motivate methods that reduce parameter count and accelerate inference. In response, model pruning emerges as an effective strategy, yet current methods typically focus on a single dimension-depth or width. We introduce MoP (Mixture of Pruners), an iterative framework that unifies these dimensions. At each iteration, MoP generates two branches-pruning in depth versus pruning in width-and selects a candidate to advance the path. On LLaMA-2 and LLaMA-3, MoP advances the frontier of structured pruning, exceeding the accuracy of competing methods across a broad set of compression regimes. It also consistently outperforms depth-only and width-only pruning. Furthermore, MoP translates structural pruning into real speedup, reducing end-to-end latency by 39% at 40% compression. Finally, extending MoP to the vision-language model LLaVA-1.5, we notably improve computational efficiency and demonstrate that text-only recovery fine-tuning can restore performance even on visual tasks.
candidates.reason: 深さ方向と幅方向の枝刈りを反復的に混合するMixture of PrunersによりLLMを構造化圧縮し、40%圧縮時にEnd-to-End遅延を39%削減する実測を示しており、LLM推論高速化への直接貢献が要旨で確認できる。

candidates.title: Scalable Context Orchestration for Serving LLMs Over Voice
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the ACM SIGOPS 32nd Symposium on Operating Systems Principles
candidates.abstract: Voice AI applications are gaining popularity as advances in large language models (LLMs) enable more natural and accessible spoken interactions. Serving these applications requires accounting not only for what users say, but also for how they speak (e.g., speaking rate) and the conditions under which their audio is captured and transmitted (e.g., background noise and packet loss). However, existing LLM systems represent conversation context as a flat, growing sequence of messages, leaving voice-specific context implicit in the audio. As a result, they can generate responses that are poorly aligned with user preferences, degrade interaction quality under adverse environmental conditions, and incur high costs over long voice sessions. We present llmovoice, a context-management middleware that explicitly models voice context and orchestrates its use. At each turn, llmovoice constructs a bounded voice context from the current user input, relevant interaction history, and explicit paralinguistic and environmental states. It then uses the serving LLM to reason over this context and generate runtime directives that guide how the system responds. We evaluate llmovoice on real-world voice applications and benchmarks. It reduces speaking-rate alignment error by 52.4%, lowers the false-interruption rate from 46.0% to 0.9% under packet loss, and reduces model usage cost by 79.2%. For long sessions, llmovoice reduces per-turn cost by up to 24.9× while retaining up to 98.7% of baseline answer quality.
candidates.reason: 音声対話向けLLMサービングで会話文脈を平坦なメッセージ列として扱う問題に対し、発話速度や雑音等の音声文脈を有界に編成するミドルウェアllmovoiceを提案しコストと割込み率を削減しており、LLMサービングへの直接貢献が確認できる。

candidates.title: FUPS: Fusion-Based Parallel Structured Pruning for Large Language Models
candidates.venue: International Conference on Parallel and Distributed Systems
candidates.abstract: Model pruning is an effective technique to reduce the dependency of neural networks on hardware resources while maintaining their performance, especially for Large Language Models(LLMs) with ever-increasing parameter scales. However, existing structured pruning methods often struggle to retain satisfactory performance under high sparsity ratios and exhibit inefficiencies when applied to ultra-large models. To address these limitations, we propose a novel structured pruning algorithm, Fusion-Based Parallel Structured Pruning (FUPS), which is simple, efficient, and easy to deploy. Its effectiveness stems from two key innovations: (1) a block-wise mechanism that partitions matrices into smaller sub-blocks to enable finer-grained redundancy identification and enhance parallel processing across accelerators; (2) a fusion mechanism that mitigates the adverse impact of knowledge space fragmentation introduced by the block mechanism, thereby enhancing the robustness and generalization capability of the matrix representation. We conduct extensive experiments on various models, and the results show that FUPS consistently preserves model performance across different sparsity settings and outperforms existing methods such as LLMPruner, Wanda, and FLAP on multiple benchmark tasks. The code is released at https://github.com/Qsiny/FUPS.
candidates.reason: 行列をサブブロックに分割して冗長性を細粒度に特定し並列処理する融合型構造化枝刈りFUPSをLLM向けに提案し、高疎性でも性能を保ちハードウェア資源依存を下げるため、LLM圧縮・推論効率化への直接貢献が確認できる。

candidates.title: Adaptive LLM Routing for Scientific Workflows: Predicting Query Complexity to Optimize Cost
candidates.venue: IEEE International Performance, Computing, and Communications Conference
candidates.abstract: Scientific workflows increasingly incorporate large-language-model (LLM) services for tasks such as metadata curation, code generation, and interactive analysis. However, inference cost in terms of resource usage varies widely with query complexity, both for service-based or self-hosted setups. Current “always-XL” deployments tend to over-provision: they safeguard response quality but squander compute usage. We introduce a routing framework based on query complexity estimations that trains a lightweight classifier on past multi-model performance data to predict the smallest model likely to satisfy a target quality threshold and then routes queries accordingly. Evaluated on $\text{4 0, 0 0 4}$ Mix-Instruct prompts, our method matches an XL-only baseline ($+0.27 \%$ quality) while reducing floating-point operations by 12.9 %, achieving competitive performance at a fraction of the cost. The method thus enables scalable, complexity-aware routing for LLM services within data- and compute-intensive scientific workflows.
candidates.reason: 科学ワークフロー向けにクエリ複雑度を軽量分類器で予測し、品質閾値を満たす最小のモデルへルーティングする枠組みを提案し、XL単独と同等品質で推論コストを削減しており、LLMルーティング・サービング最適化への直接貢献が確認できる。
